verdict.rationale: Mirrors' own corrections (routed context changes) can be reviewed and rolled back. Its docs describe previewing a correction against stored traces before activation, then keeping, revising, or rolling back the change after comparing outcomes with holdout sessions. Explicit version history is not documented, and corrections are routed context edits rather than general automations. Missing for 10: documented version history or diffs of corrections, details of how rollback works, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Preview your routing conditions against stored traces to review matches, misses, and unexpected matches before activation.
Keep what helps, revise what doesn’t, or roll back a change.
Mirrors previews each correction against your stored conversations, so you see every one it would have reached, including any you didn’t expect, before you turn it on.
You or your coding agent write the correction and choose when to activate it.
